question: A program calls sleep(1000) in its main loop on battery power. What happens to the board's current draw during the sleep?
options: It stays near the awake level
It drops to the Deep Sleep floor until the second has passed
It drops to zero because the CPU stops
It halves, because the display is switched off
explanation: sleep() waits in On mode; only power.deep_sleep() turns on-board components off. Misconception: 'sleep' means low power.

question: write_analog(511) with a 20 ms period drives an LED. What voltage does the LED see at any instant?
options: About 3.3 V or 0 V, switching
A steady 1.65 V
A steady 2.33 V, the RMS value
A voltage that ramps smoothly from 0 V up to 3.3 V
explanation: PWM switches between the rails; only the average over a period is 1.65 V. Misconception: PWM is an analog voltage.

question: A 16-bit register holds 0xFFFF. What signed value is it?
explanation: Two's complement: 0xFFFF = 65535 - 65536 = -1. Sign-magnitude would read it as -32767, and -32768 is 0x8000. Misconception: the top bit is just a minus sign.

question: You average 1,000 readings of a perfectly steady 1.000 V with a noise-free 10-bit ADC. What do you get?
options: Exactly 1.000 V, because errors average out
The same rounded value: the error does not average out
A value within 0.03 mV of 1.000 V
A value spread randomly across one whole quantisation step
explanation: With no noise every reading has the same deterministic rounding error; the Delta^2/12 model needs a busy input or dither.

question: A light sensor sampled at 30 Hz shows a 10 Hz flicker under mains lighting. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The lamp really flickers at 10 Hz
A faster flicker aliased down to 10 Hz
The sensor's 0-255 range distorts the signal
Radio interference coupling in from another micro:bit board
explanation: 100 Hz sampled at 30 Hz appears at |100 - 90| = 10 Hz. Misconception: what the samples show is what happened.

question: Which statement about averaging N noisy samples is correct?
options: Noise always falls by a factor N
Independent noise falls by sqrt(N); drift falls less
Noise always falls by sqrt(N), whatever its kind
Averaging removes noise of every kind and never delays the signal
explanation: The sqrt(N) law needs independence; correlated drift does not average out, and every average adds delay.

question: A radio link retransmits until it gets an ack. What new failure does this create if nothing else changes?
options: Fewer delivered readings than before
Corrupted frames that pass the CRC
A deadlock where each board waits for the other one forever
Duplicates, when an ack is lost
explanation: Retransmission turns loss into duplication; the receiver needs sequence numbers and dedupe.

question: A frame carries a valid CRC-16. What does that tell you?
options: It was sent by a trusted board
It has not been altered by an attacker on the way
It was very probably not damaged by noise
It arrived in the right order
explanation: A CRC detects accidental errors; it is keyless and linear, so an attacker can fix it up. Authenticity needs a MAC (lesson 19).

question: Three tasks have total utilisation 0.70 on one processor. Is meeting every deadline guaranteed?
options: Yes, because 0.70 is below 1
No, because utilisation must be below 0.5
Only under assumptions such as preemption
Yes, as long as the task with the shortest period always runs first
explanation: The RM bound for 3 tasks is 0.78 but assumes preemptive, independent tasks; a cooperative loop adds blocking.

question: A heater controller uses proportional control only. What happens to the temperature at steady state?
options: It reaches the set-point exactly
It oscillates forever
It settles short of the set-point
It overshoots and stays above the set-point
explanation: P control leaves e = r/(1 + K Kp); integral action is needed for zero error.

question: Doubling the proportional gain of a stable discrete loop will always...
options: ...make the loop respond faster and keep it stable whatever the plant
...reduce the error, but may destabilise the loop
...remove the steady-state error
...have no effect once the loop is stable
explanation: Error falls with gain, but the pole a - b Kp leaves the unit circle beyond (1 + a)/b.

question: Your battery model gives 9,600 h, a teammate's gives 9,588 h from the same inputs. What should you check first?
options: Which of you used more decimal places
Whether the battery is alkaline or lithium
Whether the simulator ran faster than real time on one machine
Whether both average over the same window
explanation: An average depends on its window; lesson 14's model once divided by 3,607,400 ms instead of one hour.

question: A local model reads sensor telemetry and says 'the room is safe'. What should decide whether an alarm sounds?
options: Threshold code; the model only explains
The model, because it sees all the data
A majority vote between the model, the code and the teacher
The model, if its confidence is above 90 %
explanation: The course rule: code decides, the agent proposes or explains, and every agent output is checked by code.

question: Is a per-desk temperature reading personal data about a pupil?
options: Yes, if it can be linked to that pupil
No, temperature is never about a person
Only if the pupil's full name is stored in the same record
Only if it is sent outside the school
explanation: Linkability (desk + seating plan) makes it personal; a name is not required.

question: Who is the micro:bit accessibility guidance mainly addressing when it suggests USB instead of Bluetooth pairing?
options: Schools without wireless networks
Pupils who cannot use a keyboard
Teachers worried about radio interference between neighbouring boards
Pupils who cannot see the LED pairing pattern
explanation: Pairing relies on seeing an LED pattern; USB transfer avoids it.
